latent_mechanisms.display_name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae replication burden in respiratory epithelium
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Cell-wall-less bacterium adheres via P1 adhesin to ciliated respiratory epithelium and replicates extracellularly; central upstream driver of all downstream pulmonary and systemic mechanisms.
Direct epithelial injury and ciliostasis from adhesion plus local cytokine release produces persistent dry cough that long outlasts pathogen burden.

Lymphoplasmacytic peribronchovascular infiltrate produces the classic atypical reticulonodular / patchy interstitial pattern, often with peribronchial thickening, sometimes lobar consolidation, and discordance between mild physical exam and impressive imaging (the 'walking pneumonia' hallmark).

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Community-Acquired Respiratory Distress Syndrome (CARDS) toxin injury
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: ADP-ribosylating CARDS toxin causes vacuolation, ciliostasis, eosinophilic airway inflammation, and bronchiolar epithelial injury; correlates with severity and with refractory / fulminant disease.
Mycoplasma triggers wheeze and asthma exacerbations through epithelial damage, IgE responses, and cytokine release; clinically meaningful especially in atopic and pediatric patients.

In refractory MPP a Th1 / IL-18 / IFN-γ-skewed cytokine storm drives persistent fever despite appropriate antibiotics, lobar consolidation with necrosis, large pleural effusion, atelectasis, and serum LDH and ferritin elevation; this is the population that benefits from corticosteroids.
TNF/IL-6/IL-1 mediated fever, malaise, headache, sore throat, myalgia, and prominent fatigue characteristic of atypical pneumonia presentation.

Anti–I-antigen IgM cross-reactive antibodies form at low temperatures, agglutinate red cells, fix complement, and produce subclinical to severe cold-type AIHA; classically peaks during the second to third week.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Mycoplasma-induced rash and mucositis (MIRM) / SJS-like reaction
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Immune complex / cross-reactive antibody and complement-mediated mucocutaneous injury with prominent mucositis (oral, ocular, urogenital) and sparse cutaneous lesions; classically in adolescents and young men.

Encephalitis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, transverse myelitis, cerebellitis, and Guillain-Barré-like syndromes mediated by molecular mimicry against galactocerebroside and other glycolipids; can occur with mild or absent respiratory disease.
Direct or immune-mediated cardiac inflammation, rare but important; presents with chest pain, troponin elevation, and ECG/echocardiographic changes.
Mild transaminase elevation common in symptomatic MPP, mostly self-limited; rarely cholestatic or severe.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Plastic bronchitis / mucus airway cast formation
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Severe bronchial mucus plugging with cast formation, especially in pediatric severe MPP; produces lobar atelectasis, ventilation defect, and may require bronchoscopic therapeutic lavage.
Severe pediatric or refractory MPP can leave fixed small-airway obliterative scarring with persistent obstructive lung disease months to years after acute illness.

23S rRNA domain V point mutations (commonly A2063G, A2064G) confer high-level macrolide resistance; prevalence is very high in East Asia (often 70–90%) and rising elsewhere; manifests as persistent fever and progressive imaging despite ≥72 h appropriate macrolide therapy.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Accumulated lung and systemic injury from delayed active therapy
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Persistent uncontrolled pathogen burden or macrolide-resistant disease after ineffective initial therapy permits progressive airway, alveolar, and extrapulmonary inflammatory injury before active therapy or immunomodulation is started.
Post-infectious immune-mediated mono- or oligoarthritis, typically large joints, weeks after infection; uncommon.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pathogen adhesion to ciliated epithelium directly initiates tracheobronchial inflammation and ciliostasis.
Distal extension of infection into peribronchovascular interstitium drives the atypical pneumonia pattern.
CARDS toxin is produced in proportion to bacterial load and drives downstream airway and parenchymal injury.
TLR2 / lipoprotein-driven innate response generates fever, malaise, and headache typical of atypical pneumonia.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: delayed B-cell autoantibody response against I antigen
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Polyclonal IgM cold agglutinins form against red-cell I-antigen after about 1–2 weeks of antigenic exposure.
Cross-reactive antibody / immune complex deposition produces mucositis-predominant cutaneous reaction.

Postinfectious immune-mediated arthritis, days to weeks after acute illness.
